name: Hoh River
gaugeName: Hoh River at US Highway 101 near Forks
blurb: Milky glacial river out of the Hoh Rain Forest in Olympic National Park.

sections.notes: A long glacial-river outing with wood and changing channels. NPS identifies Hoh Campground as a popular Class II put-in and warns of log jams; scout and check current local conditions. The separate entrance-station put-in is not substituted here. The retained 20-mile planning distance is preliminary, and no reviewed live float-time model is assigned. The park launch and DNR take-out have separate entrance and parking/pass requirements.

notices.title: Hoh access reopened — check before travel
notices.text: NPS lists Upper Hoh Road open with a November 13, 2026 status date and Hoh Campground open when checked November 16. DNR lists Hoh Oxbow Campground open. Storms can change access; recheck the agency pages and your shuttle before departure.
notices.sourceName: National Park Service — current road conditions

notices.title: Log jams and changing channels
notices.text: NPS warns of log jams on the Hoh. A campground being open does not establish a clear river route or usable water-edge landing. Scout and obtain current local river information.

sections.routeReview: Access-area map only. The markers identify the NPS and DNR campground facilities, not exact water-edge landings. A continuous river course, shore connectors and current passage through log jams have not been approved.

putInAccess.operator: National Park Service — Olympic National Park
putInAccess.sourceName: National Park Service — Olympic boating guidance and current conditions
putInAccess.note: NPS lists Upper Hoh Road open with a November 13, 2026 status date, and Hoh Campground open when checked November 16. Recreation.gov supplies the campground-area coordinate. Satellite context shows the campsite complex beside the river but cannot establish an exact current landing or navigable channel. NPS identifies log-jam hazards. The separate entrance-station put-in is not this facility.
putInAccess.directions: Follow Upper Hoh Road from US 101 to the signed Hoh Campground inside Olympic National Park. NPS lists this campground as a popular river put-in. Identify the permitted water-edge approach on foot and check current river conditions before launching; this marker identifies the campground area, not a surveyed landing.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: Washington DNR — Olympic Peninsula recreation and campsite status
takeOutAccess.note: DNR explicitly lists Hoh Oxbow Open when checked November 16, 2026. Historical bridge-work alerts with October end dates remain on two DNR pages; those expired date ranges alone are not the basis for reopening. The original agency campground-area coordinate is retained. River-side trees, side channels and changing banks prevent an exact landing claim.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the signed DNR Hoh Oxbow Campground approach near the US 101 Hoh River bridge. Identify the designated boat-access approach before starting the float. The marker identifies the campground area, not the exact landing; confirm current signs, road status and parking/pass requirements.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

mapAuditNote: Agency-listed campground access areas reviewed after reopening. Exact water-edge landings remain pending; this is not an exact river-access audit.
